items.definition: To take air in slowly and let it out slowly.
items.example: Breathe in, and blow out slowly.

items.definition: A person you like and who likes you back. Friends like to spend time together.
items.example: Minh is my best friend.

items.definition: Letting somebody use your things, and letting them do things with you too.
items.example: We shared the ball all afternoon.

items.definition: One person goes first, and then the other one goes. It is how two people share one thing fairly.
items.example: We took turns on the swing.

items.definition: Giving your full attention to somebody who is talking.
items.example: He listened to my whole story.

items.definition: When two friends get angry with each other. Every friendship has these.
items.example: We had a quarrel and made up the same afternoon.

items.definition: What you need from somebody else. You can need help with a task, a feeling or a person.
items.example: I need some help with this.

items.definition: To say out loud that you need it. It is not the same as complaining.
items.example: I asked for help and she came straight away.

items.definition: An adult who looks after children, like a parent, a teacher or the school nurse.
items.example: I told a grown-up about it.

items.definition: To make a small attempt before you ask for help.
items.example: I tried first, and then I asked.

items.definition: Polite and friendly towards other people, even when you do not like their food.
items.example: It is kind to say thank you for the food.

items.definition: A nice thing you say about what somebody did or made.
items.example: I gave her a compliment about her picture.

items.definition: To ask somebody to join you, and to accept it when they say no.
items.example: I invited him to sit with us.

items.definition: To make room for somebody in the group, the game or the talk.
items.example: We included the new boy in our game.

items.definition: Something done or thought wrongly.
items.example: Use it when a mistake costs time or a retry.

items.definition: To taste a food for the first time. One small bite is enough for today.
items.example: I will try one bite of the soup.

items.definition: To make something right or better after it went wrong.
items.example: I fixed the picture with a new sheet of paper.

items.definition: To say sorry and show that you understand what you did wrong.
items.example: I apologised to my sister for shouting.

items.definition: A small mistake that happens because you were busy or in a hurry.
items.example: That was just a slip.

items.definition: To have or use a thing with others.
To play first and then let the next person play.
items.example: We take turns on the slide.

items.definition: To stay calm and do something else until your turn comes.
items.example: I wait until my friend finishes the puzzle.

items.definition: To give one thing away and get a different thing back.
items.example: I trade my ball for your dinosaur.

items.definition: The polite word you say after somebody helps you or gives you something.
items.example: Thank you for lending me your ruler.

items.definition: The word you say when you did something wrong. It shows you take responsibility.
items.example: Sorry, I stepped on your foot.

items.definition: The polite way to get somebody's attention or to pass by them.
items.example: Excuse me, may I get past?

items.definition: A careful, grown-up way to ask for something. People listen more when you use it.
items.example: May I sit here, please?

items.definition: Something that happens inside you. It shows on your face and tells you what you need.
items.example: My feeling today is happy.

items.definition: A warm, good feeling inside. It makes you want to smile and share.
items.example: I feel happy when my friend sits with me.

items.definition: A heavy feeling inside. It often wants tears or quiet time.
items.example: I feel sad because my cat is away.

items.definition: An afraid feeling. Your heart beats fast and you want to run or hide.
items.example: I feel scared in the dark, so I hold my blanket.

items.definition: Wheat grain ground into a fine powder. It is the main part of the bread.
items.example: Flour is made from wheat at the mill.

items.definition: A tiny living fungus that eats sugar in the flour and makes gas.
items.example: We woke up the yeast in warm water for ten minutes.

items.definition: The soft, sticky mix of flour and water before it is baked.
items.example: I put the dough in a bowl and covered it.

items.definition: Pushing and folding the dough so it becomes smooth and strong.
items.example: Kneading the dough for five minutes feels strange at first.

items.definition: The resting time when the dough grows bigger because of the yeast.
items.example: The dough is proving now, so it will be ready in an hour.

items.definition: The first meal of the day, eaten after you wake up.
items.example: Breakfast is ready, so please sit down.

items.definition: The feeling you get when your body wants food and needs energy.
items.example: I am hungry, so I will have some bread.

items.definition: Grain that you pour into milk and eat with a spoon.
items.example: I ate cereal with cold milk.

items.definition: Bread that is warmed until it is brown and crisp.
items.example: I put jam on my toast.
